name: Barbarian
description: Fierce warriors defined by primal rage—supernatural strength, resilience, and instinct. (Full layout below mirrors reference class pages.)

descriptionSections.body:
A tall human tribesman strides through a blizzard, draped in fur and hefting his axe. He laughs as he charges toward the frost giant who dared poach his people's elk herd.

A half-orc snarls at the latest challenger to her authority over their tribe, ready to break his neck with her bare hands as she did to the last six rivals.

Frothing at the mouth, a dwarf slams his helmet into the face of his drow foe, then turns to drive his armored elbow into the gut of another.

These barbarians, different as they might be, are defined by their rage: unbridled, unquenchable, and unthinking fury. More than a mere emotion, their anger is the ferocity of a cornered predator, the unrelenting assault of a storm, the churning turmoil of the sea.

For some, their rage springs from a communion with fierce animal spirits. Others draw from a roiling reservoir of anger at a world full of pain. For every barbarian, rage is a power that fuels not just a battle frenzy but also uncanny reflexes, resilience, and feats of strength.

Barbarians come alive in the chaos of combat. They can enter a berserk state where rage takes over, giving them superhuman strength and resilience. A barbarian can draw on this reservoir of fury only a few times without resting, but those few rages are usually sufficient to defeat whatever threats arise.

descriptionSections.heading: Primal Instinct
descriptionSections.body: People of towns and cities take pride in their settled ways, as if denying one's connection to nature were a mark of superiority. To a barbarian, though, a settled life is no virtue, but a sign of weakness. The strong embrace nature—valuing keen instincts, primal physicality, and ferocious rage. Barbarians are uncomfortable when hedged in by walls and crowds. They thrive in the wilds of their homelands: the tundra, jungle, or grasslands where their tribes live and hunt.

descriptionSections.heading: A Life of Danger
descriptionSections.body:
A barbarian plays an important role as a protector of their people and a leader in times of war. Life in the wild places of the world is fraught with peril: rival tribes, deadly weather, and terrifying monsters. Barbarians charge headlong into that danger so that their people don't have to.

Their courage in the face of danger makes barbarians perfectly suited for adventuring. Wandering is often a way of life for their native tribes, and the rootless life of the adventurer is little hardship for a barbarian. Some barbarians miss the close-knit family structures of the tribe, but eventually find them replaced by the bonds formed among the members of their adventuring parties.

descriptionSections.heading: Creating a Barbarian
descriptionSections.body:
When creating a barbarian character, think about where your character comes from and his or her place in the world. Talk with your DM about an appropriate origin for your barbarian. Did you come from a distant land, making you a stranger in the area of the campaign? Or is the campaign set in a rough-and-tumble frontier where barbarians are common?

What led you to take up the adventuring life? Were you lured to settled lands by the promise of riches? Did you join forces with soldiers of those lands to face a shared threat? Did monsters or an invading horde drive you out of your homeland, making you a rootless refugee? Perhaps you were a prisoner of war, brought in chains to another land and only now able to win your freedom. Or you might have been cast out from your people because of a crime you committed, a taboo you violated, or a coup that removed you from a position of authority.

descriptionSections.heading: Quick Build
descriptionSections.body: You can make a barbarian quickly by following these suggestions. First, put your highest ability score in Strength, followed by Constitution. Second, choose the outlander background.

feature.name: Rage
feature.description: On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging (if you aren’t wearing heavy armor): advantage on Strength checks and saves; when you hit with a melee weapon attack using Strength, bonus damage per the Rage Damage table; resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage; you can’t cast or concentrate on spells. Rage lasts 1 minute and ends early if unconscious, you end it, or you neither attacked a hostile creature nor took damage since your last turn. Uses per long rest as shown in the Rages column of the class table.

feature.name: Unarmored Defense
feature.description: While not wearing armor, your AC equals 10 + Dexterity modifier + Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

feature.name: Reckless Attack
feature.description: When you make your first attack on your turn, you can attack recklessly to gain advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength this turn; attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

feature.name: Danger Sense
feature.description: You have advantage on Dexterity saves against visible effects (like traps and spells), unless you are blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

feature.name: Primal Path
feature.description: You choose a path that shapes your rage (e.g. Berserker, Totem Warrior). Your choice grants features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 (max 20), or take a feat if your game uses optional feats.

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.description: When you take the Attack action, you can attack twice.

feature.name: Fast Movement
feature.description: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

feature.name: Path Feature
feature.description: You gain a feature from your Primal Path.

feature.name: Feral Instinct
feature.description: Advantage on initiative. If surprised at the start of combat and not incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn if you enter your rage before doing anything else.

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 (max 20), or take a feat if your game uses optional feats.

feature.name: Brutal Critical
feature.description: On a critical hit with a melee attack, roll one additional weapon damage die. This improves to two extra dice at 13th level and three at 17th level.

feature.name: Path Feature
feature.description: You gain a feature from your Primal Path.

feature.name: Relentless Rage
feature.description: If you drop to 0 HP while raging (and don’t die outright), you can make a DC 10 Constitution save; on a success you stay at 1 HP. Each later use raises the DC by 5; resets after a short or long rest.

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 (max 20), or take a feat if your game uses optional feats.

feature.name: Brutal Critical (2 dice)
feature.description: On a melee critical hit, roll two additional weapon damage dice.

feature.name: Path Feature
feature.description: You gain a feature from your Primal Path.

feature.name: Persistent Rage
feature.description: Your rage ends early only if you fall unconscious or you choose to end it.

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 (max 20), or take a feat if your game uses optional feats.

feature.name: Brutal Critical (3 dice)
feature.description: On a melee critical hit, roll three additional weapon damage dice.

feature.name: Indomitable Might
feature.description: If your total on a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use your Strength score in place of the total.

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two scores by 1 (max 20), or take a feat if your game uses optional feats.

feature.name: Primal Champion
feature.description: Strength and Constitution increase by 4; maximum for those scores becomes 24. Your rages are unlimited.
